صَقْبٌ The young one of a camel: (M, L, K:) and so سَقْبٌ [q. v.]: (M:) but the latter is the more chaste, and some have rejected the former word: (MF:) pl. صِقَابٌ and صُقْبَانٌ (M, K) [and app. صُقُوبٌ also, like سُقُوبٌ,] and [pl. of pauc.] أَصْقُبٌ. (TA.) ―
-b2- And Anything [i. e. any animal] tall, together with plumpness, or with fatness, softness, thinness of the skin, and plumpness; (S, M, K;) and so with س; (M;) as also ↓ صَقَبٌ . (TA.) Applied to a branch, Juicy, thick, and long. (TA.) ―
-b3- And A tent-pole: (M, K:) or the middle tent-pole, which is the longest: (S, M, K:) and so with س: (M:) pl. صُقُوبٌ. (S, M, K.) [See also this pl. below.] ―
-b4- And The fist: so in the phrase ضَرَبَهُ بِصَقْبِهِ [expl. above]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
